skill.name: ai-audio-generation
skill.description: AI audio generation for agents through Image Skill's hosted creative runtime. It helps create music, sound effects, ambience, and durable hosted audio from text prompts.
skill.summary: Generate hosted AI audio from text prompts through Image Skill.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: The skill is a hosted audio-generation wrapper that intentionally instructs agents to run npm-based CLI commands and contact Image Skill's hosted API. Most markdown backtick hits are false positives, but the unpinned npx workflow, global skill installs, hidden agent-state writes, and remote next-command guidance create meaningful execution and trust risks. No prompt-injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin image-skill and skills package versions, document expected package hashes, and avoid @latest in marketplace instructions.
Require human review and an allowlist for any data.next_command before execution, even when copy_runnable is true.
Ask for explicit consent before changing HOME, CODEX_HOME, or installing global agent skills, and explain the affected directories.

remediation.issue: Hosted API data and spend exposure
remediation.suggestion: Disclose what prompts, media, job metadata, and payment data are sent to Image Skill, and require approval before paid generation.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses inline markdown code to name the image-skill runtime and does not instruct shell execution. The external service risk is addressed by separate network and command findings.
Line 28 tells agents to run a data.next_command value from the hosted workflow when a flag is true. That is a remote command handoff and should be reviewed before execution.
Lines 32-34 include an npx command that executes image-skill@latest from npm. Unpinned remote package execution can run changed code without local review.
Lines 34-38 contain a closing markdown fence, a heading, and an opening fence, not an executable command. The adjacent real commands have separate findings.
Lines 38-40 include the main npx image-skill@latest create command. It executes a remote npm package and can initiate hosted generation and spending.
Lines 40-46 are markdown fence and explanatory text before the install command. The command itself is covered by the finding starting at line 46.
Lines 46-48 instruct running npx skills add with global Codex installation flags. This executes remote tooling and modifies agent skill state.
Lines 48-52 only close a markdown fence, introduce the canonical entry, and open another fence. The following command is covered by the line 52 finding.
Lines 52-54 instruct running npx skills add for the canonical image-skill entry with global Codex flags. It can install or alter agent-visible skills.
Lines 54-59 are markdown closure and prose about writable skill state, not a direct command. Hidden state risk is handled by filesystem findings.
Line 59 references HOME and CODEX_HOME paths in inline markdown. It does not execute a shell command at that line.
Lines 62-67 contain export, mkdir, and npx skills add commands. They change HOME/CODEX_HOME for the install and run remote package tooling.
The range includes later guidance to run image-skill feedback create --json after fallback use. It is a lower-confidence command finding because most of the range is markdown text.
Line 5 is homepage metadata for the skill. It does not by itself cause a network request or data transfer.
Line 6 is a documentation URL in metadata. This is informational rather than an automatic network operation.
Line 10 points to the canonical skill document. It is a reference URL, not a hidden or unauthorized network call.
Line 11 declares the hosted API endpoint used by the skill. The domain is disclosed, but user prompts and job data may be sent to an external service.
Line 73 lists a public skill document URL under Shared Contract. This is documentation linkage, not executable network behavior.
Line 74 lists the LLM contract URL for reference. It does not direct automatic exfiltration or background network access.
Line 75 lists the CLI contract URL. This is a transparent documentation reference, not a network call.
Line 76 lists the hosted API endpoint that the runtime depends on. This disclosed third-party service can receive prompts, job metadata, and generated media context.
Line 59 states that the Codex adapter writes to $HOME/.agents and uses CODEX_HOME for profile state. Writing hidden agent state can affect future agent behavior.
Line 63 sets HOME to a hidden workspace directory before installation. Redirecting HOME changes where tools write credentials, config, and skill state.
Line 64 sets CODEX_HOME to a hidden .codex directory. That explicitly changes Codex profile state storage and should require user awareness.

content.user_title: Generate AI Audio with a Hosted Runtime
content.value_statement: Creative teams need fast audio drafts without managing provider accounts or local models. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create hosted audio with recoverable jobs and cost receipts.
actual_capabilities: Routes text-to-audio prompts through the Image Skill hosted runtime.
Provides guide-mode and generation commands for an audio model.
Supports durable hosted audio URLs, recoverable jobs, and cost receipts.
Includes install guidance for Codex and the canonical Image Skill entry.
Offers a feedback path when a required audio capability is missing.
limitations: Requires network access to Image Skill and npm package sources.
Audio quality and model availability depend on the hosted runtime.
Paid media generation may occur after readiness checks and approval.
Does not provide local model execution or provider-specific editing tools.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Audio
use_cases.description: Create short music beds or interface sounds for early product reviews.

use_cases.title: Prepare Campaign Sound Ideas
use_cases.description: Generate draft audio directions for ads, launches, and social videos.

use_cases.title: Generate Scene Ambience
use_cases.description: Create background ambience and effects for games, stories, or videos.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Audio Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a quick first result.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-audio-generation to create a 10 second warm ambient loop for a calm onboarding screen. Start with the guide before spending.

prompt_templates.title: Design Sound Effects
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a focused sound design task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three short sound effect concepts for a successful file upload. Keep them subtle, modern, and suitable for an office product.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Creative Directions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for selecting between styles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create two audio directions for a product launch teaser: one minimal electronic bed and one cinematic percussion bed. Include hosted links and cost receipts.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Production Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt with constraints and review steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the no-spend guide first, confirm missing inputs, then generate an approved 20 second ambience with a maximum estimated cost of 0.20 USD.

output_examples.input: A calm synth bed for a meditation app preview.
output_examples.output: A hosted audio draft is created with a durable link, job status, estimated cost, and a short description of the generated mood.

output_examples.input: Three notification sounds for a project management app.
output_examples.output: The agent returns multiple hosted sound options, notes their intended use, and records the generation details for later recovery.

output_examples.input: Dark rain ambience for a narrative game scene.
output_examples.output: The result includes a hosted ambience file, the model used, a receipt, and guidance for requesting a revision if needed.

best_practices: Start with guide mode and confirm readiness before paid generation.
Describe duration, mood, instruments, pacing, and intended use.
Review hosted links, costs, and command details before sharing outputs.
anti_patterns: Do not run paid generation without explicit user approval.
Do not paste provider keys, secrets, or private credentials into prompts.
Do not execute remote suggested commands in sensitive environments without review.

faq.question: Does this skill require provider API keys?
faq.answer: No. It uses the Image Skill hosted runtime and an optional Image Skill token.

faq.question: Can it generate music and sound effects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is intended for music, ambience, sound effects, and text-to-audio prompts.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. It requires network access to npm sources and the Image Skill hosted service.

faq.question: Can generation cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide helps avoid spend until inputs are ready, but approved generation can use paid media credits.

faq.question: Are outputs recoverable later?
faq.answer: The skill describes durable hosted URLs, recoverable jobs, and cost receipts for generated work.

faq.question: What should I review before running it?
faq.answer: Review any npx command, hosted API use, spend limits, and changes to HOME or CODEX_HOME.
